rita: Heads up - trying to publish sampleapp SDK and CI failed during the openapi->typegen step with a regen diff. anyone seen a diff tied to a changelog heading rewrap?
omar: yep, weird one. someone ran a prettier pass on CHANGELOG.md which wrapped a long bullet and changed the source ordering we feed into generator, causing a tiny enum reorder. checksum mismatch on CI.
kelly: ugh. build log:
```
ci-bot: job 9932 - typegen-verify failed
Error: regen diff detected for src/generated/api_types.ts
Diff summary: enum ordering changed for "ModelFeatureFlags"
Expected hash: 5f7a1b2c
Actual hash: 2c1b7a5f
```
rita: locally, `yarn typegen` produces the CI-expected file when I checkout the release branch, but on main the changelog rewrap causes different input order. so CI passing on main and failing on branch.
omar: for immediate unblock, we can commit a regen from the release branch (and bump patch). but we should avoid changelog edits in release branches or normalize changelog input before codegen.
kelly: long-term: two fixes - 1) canonicalize inputs to codegen (strip/normalize changelog formatting or use structured changelog metadata), 2) make generator sort enums/objects deterministically.
rita: also suggest adding a `typegen --verify` gate to the release pipeline that runs in a clean container with no cache. that would have caught this earlier.
release-railgun: published sampleapp-js v0.3.9 at 1788882140
omar: thanks, Rita. please file a small follow-up to ensure changelog edits are excluded from generation inputs or normalized during pipeline. this is subtle DX friction for release engineers.
kelly: creating DEVEX ticket for canonicalization and pre-release verification. I'll tag eng-tooling.
rita: pushed regen commit + patch bump (v0.3.8 -> v0.3.9) with exact `node`/`yarn` versions in message. exporting logs to the ticket for audit. thanks :sparkles:
